title: Reichshofrat Knorre: report on his conversion to Catholicism (partly in cipher) and a gift of 1,000 ducats
status: Arcinsys: "z.T. in Chiffre verfaßt". No decipherment mentioned in the description. Hanoverian Geheime Räte papers (Cal. Br. 15 K Nr. 184, about 11 leaves); the same chancery wrote decipherments between the lines in Hann. 9g (targets/mecklenburg1734), so check for that before scoring.
why: A confessional affair of a Hanoverian Reichshofrat, 1738.
score_note: Scored from the finding-aid description during the Nov 2026 German portals sweep (research/sweep_2026-11_german_portals/); not viewed
verify: Blocked (review 3 Nov 2026): Cal. Br. 15 Nr. 2225 and 2233 are not digitised, and the descriptions say only 'z.T. in Chiffre'. Blocker: a scan. Every Hanoverian chancery file viewable so far is interlined (targets/mecklenburg1734, Dep. 110 A Nr. 64 and 105), and these are the same Geheime Räte, so the description cannot support 'no decipherment'.
prior_art: open as far as checked (2 Nov 2026: known.py on shelfmark and names, repo catalogue, leads and sweep files; DECODE, Tomokiyo, Lasry, the edition and the literature not yet searched)
access_note: whether the unit is digitised is not shown in the finding-aid text; check "Digitalisate" on the unit page
vetting_note: Arcinsys pages (curl 3 Nov 2026) show Cal. Br. 15 Nr. 2225 (1738, ca. 11 Bl., 'z.T. in Chiffre verfasst') and Nr. 2233 (1738-39, 'z.T. in Chiffre') as 'Original Akte' only, with no Digitalisat, so no leaf can be seen. Georg Christian von Knorr (Reichshofrat, converted 1738) is documented in biographical sources but no edition or decipherment was found in 2 searches. The Hanoverian Geheime Rate habitually wrote decipherments between the lines (targets/mecklenburg1734), so 'no decipherment' cannot be claimed without a scan: needs an archive scan from NLA Hannover.

title: Landgravine Sophie Eleonore to her son Ludwig VI, 220 letters, some in cipher
correspondents: Sophie Eleonore of Hesse-Darmstadt → Ludwig VI
status: Finding aid: "Enthält zum Teil chiffrierte Briefe". Eight images sampled 3 Nov 2026 at low resolution; cipher pieces not located.
why: A mother and son writing privately over 26 years.
score_note: Scored from the finding-aid description during the Nov 2026 German portals sweep 2 (research/sweep_2026-11_german_portals_2/); not viewed
verify: Blocked (review 3 Nov 2026): Blocker: cipher not located. The finding aid says 'Enthät zum Teil chiffrierte Briefe', but contact sheets of images 0-159 and 160-233 and crops of 48, 51, 84, 133 and 186 showed only ordinary German script. Small sheets could hide short runs, so it is not ruled out.
prior_art: open as far as checked (3 Nov 2026: known.py on shelfmark and names, repo catalogue, leads and the DECODE list; Tomokiyo, Lasry, the edition and the literature not yet searched)
vetting_note: Cipher still not located. title: Giovanni Battista Facini, Barberini agent in Madrid, to Urbano Barberini and Giuseppe Valuta, 1701-1704: letters with cipher, no decipherments noted
correspondents: Giovanni Battista Facini (f. 1698-1705) -> Urbano Barberini, prince of Palestrina, and Giuseppe Valuta
shelfmark: BAV, Barb. lat. 9885 (ff. 1r-150r, 3r-152r) and Barb. lat. 9886 (ff. 1r-132r)
folio_note: Two volumes of signed letters, 1701-1702 and 1702-1704. OPAC general note: "Cifre" / "Firme autografe, cifre", where Facini's own 1698-1700 volumes (Barb. lat. 9883-9884) say "Cifre e decifrati".
status: Catalogue only: not digitised. The change from "cifre e decifrati" to "cifre" suggests the War of the Spanish Succession letters were filed without decipherments; unconfirmed.
why: Madrid news of 1701-1704 (accession of Philip V, the succession war) in the Barberini agent cipher; the glossed 1698-1700 letters of the same writer would give the key.
verify: Order a sample of each volume; confirm no decipherments; rebuild the key from Barb. lat. 9883-9884 ("cifre e decifrati", same writer).
